knowledge_base: Mermaid renders deterministically only when node ids are stable strings; auto-generated ids change between runs.
Graphviz dot is best for hierarchical graphs; neato suits force-directed layouts of small undirected graphs.
Edge labels should be short; long labels cause edge crossings that defeat the purpose of a diagram.
LR (left-to-right) layout reads better for pipelines; TB (top-to-bottom) reads better for class hierarchies.
Subgraphs in mermaid use 'subgraph name ... end'; nested subgraphs render but degrade with more than two levels.
Color should encode at most one dimension; using both color and shape for the same axis is wasted ink.
Mermaid live editor strips comments; keep the canonical source in the repo and treat the editor as a preview.
For diffs over time, render to SVG and commit the SVG so reviewers can see graph changes without re-rendering.
Cyclic dependency diagrams should highlight back-edges (target rank < source rank) in red to draw the eye.
When a graph has more than 50 nodes, partition by cluster (community detection) before rendering.
